statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Call an index sequence 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{m-1} < len(nums) a valid subsequence of nums for k if for every j with 0 <= j < m-1, nums[i_j] < nums[i_{j+1}] and nums[i_{j+1}] - nums[i_j] <= k. Then r is the maximum m for which a valid subsequence of nums of length m exists. Equivalently, there exists a valid subsequence of length r, and every valid subsequence has length at most r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; in particular, it does not overflow, go out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= the number of distinct values in nums, that is, the cardinality of the set {nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums)}.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a valid subsequence of nums for k of length r, where a valid subsequence is an index sequence 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{m-1} < len(nums) such that for every j with 0 <= j < m-1, nums[i_j] < nums[i_{j+1}] and nums[i_{j+1}] - nums[i_j] <= k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every valid subsequence of nums for k has length at most r, where a valid subsequence is an index sequence 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{m-1} < len(nums) such that for every j with 0 <= j < m-1, nums[i_j] < nums[i_{j+1}] and nums[i_{j+1}] - nums[i_j] <= k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] < nums[i+1] and nums[i+1] - nums[i] <= k.

statement: Whenever length_of_lis(nums, k1) returns a result r1 and length_of_lis(nums, k2) returns a result r2, we have r1 <= r2.
preconditions: For the same slice nums, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k1 <= 100000; 1 <= k2 <= 100000; k1 <= k2.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the largest m for which there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{m-1} < len(nums) with nums[j_t] < nums[j_{t+1}] for every t with 0 <= t < m-1 (a longest strictly increasing subsequence ignoring the adjacent-difference condition).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000; k >= max(nums) - min(nums), where max(nums) and min(nums) are the maximum and minimum of all elements of nums.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000; for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and nums[i] < nums[j], we have nums[j] - nums[i] > k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 2 if and only if there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), nums[i] < nums[j], and nums[j] - nums[i] <= k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Let nums+c be the slice of the same length with (nums+c)[i] = nums[i] + c for every i. Whenever length_of_lis(nums, k) returns a result r and length_of_lis(nums+c, k) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000; c is an integer such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] + c <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of indices l and u with 0 <= l <= u < len(nums) such that for every i with l <= i < u, nums[i] < nums[i+1] and nums[i+1] - nums[i] <= k, we have r >= u - l + 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the largest m for which there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{m-1} < len(nums) with nums[j_t] < nums[j_{t+1}] for every t with 0 <= t < m-1 (the ordinary strictly increasing subsequence length without the adjacent-difference condition).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 100000.
